scenes.text: Trade-offs: earlier is not always faster
Study the costs alongside the benefits, rather than increasing every budget.
Proposal pp. 1–2 | Planned experiments; results pending
Less waiting versus more tokens accepted per verification.
More handoff chances versus events, packing, and synchronization.
Better coverage versus memory and discarded draft work.
Measure savings after controller and in-flight drain costs.

notes: Sweep publication checkpoints, maximum depth, candidate/fan-out budgets and execution-shape buckets on tuning data. Compare equal total work/candidate budgets where meaningful, report actual GPU cost and memory, and freeze winners before final evaluation. Earlier handoff can reduce target waiting but also reduce useful tokens per verification. Frequent publication adds events, packing and synchronization. More branches increase coverage and consume memory or draft work. A controller can improve choices yet lose end-to-end after its decision overhead. Record discarded/obsolete draft token work and actual kernel-drain time.
title: Trade-offs: earlier is not always faster

notes: These gates update the proposal's week-based milestones without claiming missed weeks are done. Evaluation1 covers baseline status, unresolved correctness, bottleneck evidence and experimental design. Before Evaluation2 aim for a safe uniform early-publication prototype and, only if it has residual headroom, unequal-depth/adaptive scheduling with preliminary ablations. Final evaluation requires frozen held-out tests, repeated timings, confidence intervals, regressions and reproducible artifacts. If adaptive scheduling fails to improve on the simple early-handoff policy after its overhead, retain the correct simpler system and quantify the negative result.
title: Milestones are evidence gates

notes: The proposal engineering target is at least 10% lower mean full-request latency on the declared balanced held-out mix than the strongest matched tested baseline; report paired uncertainty and every family regression. This is a target, not a forecast or guaranteed win. Correctness requires token-for-token greedy equality to unchanged target AR, not tolerance-aware logit checks. Deliver runnable code, manifest/configuration versions, raw measurements, plots/traces, report, presentation and demo. Proposed ownership: Ishaan baseline integration, KV/handoff and correctness; Vishal scheduling, statistics and ablations; Eshaan publication, execution optimization and profiling. Single-request greedy decoding remains core scope; stochastic sampling and multi-request serving are outside the required experiments.
